timeline_reviews.summary: Serial main stream transport log only (4647 transport events); semantic actions are projected in the raw serial agent trajectory.
Serial parent trajectory (42 semantic events) performs all probing in one stream with Bash only and reaches timeout without a compiling implementation.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering obligation: create an original executable matching the supplied goimports-reviser binary by running it and reading bundled documentation only.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It chose a parent-plus-workflow plan: the parent did early probing and launched a workflow whose script assigned many behavioral dimensions to child agents, then planned critique and follow-up phases.
parallel.implementation: The parent began a Go reimplementation and wrote internal/reviser/imports.go and internal/reviser/reviser.go plus a module skeleton, while children produced behavioral findings under /tmp.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact contained partial internal source directories, go.mod, README, images, LICENSE, and executable, but artifact_validation.ok was false and no final response was written.
parallel.verification: The run used many black-box probes and some child reports, but did not reach a passing integrated build; the official evaluator completed and returned compile_failed with 597 tests not run.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with many child agents still in progress, only a few results recorded, and the final implementation remained incomplete enough to fail compilation.

serial.requirements: The serial run received the same clean-room reverse-engineering prompt and recognized the need to observe CLI behavior and avoid source lookup or static binary analysis.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It operated as a single agent with workflows and delegation tools disabled; all probing and reasoning stayed in the parent trajectory.
serial.implementation: It spent the run probing CLI, formatting, import ordering, project-name, and related behaviors, but no final source implementation tree comparable to the parallel internal package was present in the artifact.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact mostly preserved repository/documentation/executable files and lacked an implemented source tree; artifact_validation.ok was false and final.txt was empty.
serial.verification: The serial run performed many local Bash probes but never produced a compileable submission; the official evaluator completed with compile_failed and 597 tests not run.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The monolithic investigation reached timeout while still probing behavior, so the delivered artifact was not a working reimplementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the requirement to reimplement the binary from observed behavior only and embedded the same constraints in its workflow instructions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the identical clean-room prompt and probed the executable and README under the same restrictions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference drove the official result; the divergence was execution strategy, not prompt interpretation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the behavior search into a workflow over many dimensions, with one agent per dimension and later critic/follow-up agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents and the runtime explicitly disabled workflow/delegation tools, so all work remained in the single parent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel pursued breadth through delegated exploration; serial pursued narrower sequential probing without coordination overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child prompts carried common rules plus dimension-specific report paths under /tmp/findings, so children were framed as research/report producers rather than source implementers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated context in one trajectory, repeatedly probing behavior in-place without cross-agent handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel needed reports to return from the workflow before the parent could reduce findings into code; serial avoided handoff boundaries but had less concurrent coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel eventually created a Go module skeleton and internal reviser implementation files after extensive probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial remained in behavioral probing through its final visible raw events and its artifact listing shows no comparable implementation directories.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel got farther on source creation, while serial gathered observations but did not deliver a source tree; neither path produced a compiling program.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow returned some reports, but the journal and workflow state show many started/retried agents still in progress at kill time.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no workflow lifecycle: no child logs, no workflow calls, and only the parent trajectory was present.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unfinished result-reduction problem caused by its live workflow; serial had no child join surface but still timed out.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children used /tmp/probe and /tmp/findings while the parent wrote final workspace source files; no concrete overwrite or shared final-source collision is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not have concurrent writers; its artifact contains the repository shell, images, license, and executable but no implemented source tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The shared-state contrast is absence of collision rather than a retained write bug; the parallel problem is budget/closure rather than conflicting writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gathered several behavioral probes and child reports but did not complete an integrated build/test cycle; official evaluation failed at compile time.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed direct Bash probes but likewise never reached a compileable submission; official evaluation failed at compile time.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both failed before test execution, so verification did not create a discordant outcome; parallel had more distributed probe data but did not convert it into a working artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 37 subagents, 1,038 child tool calls, and 2,216,252 child tokens; the workflow was killed and the agent timed out at the 2,400-second budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and 40 Bash calls, but it also timed out at roughly the same wall-clock budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's budget was consumed by broad fan-out and retries before synthesis could finish; serial consumed the budget in a monolithic investigation without delegation overhead.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail, not discordant: both completed evaluations reported compile_failed, solution_passed=false, and 597 tests not run. The concrete task-solving difference is strategic. Parallel launched a large delegated exploration workflow and also began a partial Go implementation, but the workflow was killed with many child probes and retries unfinished before the parent reduced findings into a compileable deliverable. Serial kept all probing in one agent with workflows disabled, produced no comparable implementation tree, and also timed out before a compileable solution.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out consumed substantial child token/tool budget and left many agents in progress at kill time.
Parent-created source files existed, but the artifact still failed validation and official compilation.
serial_contributors: Serial control had no delegated workflow overhead but spent the full budget on sequential probing.
Serial artifact lacked a source implementation tree and failed official compilation as well.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel produced partial Go package files under internal/reviser, internal/module, internal/pkgload, internal/std, and internal/cache; serial did not show comparable source directories in the artifact.
Both attempts left an incomplete/noncompileable submission, so ordinary incompleteness rather than a discordant evaluator effect explains the shared failure.

candidates.reason: Rejected because the parallel parent explicitly owned implementation after launching probes, creating /workspace/internal/reviser and source files; the issue was unfinished execution under fan-out, not absence of an implementer.

Rejected because no separate completed component implementations required cross-agent integration; child work was behavioral research, and parent-owned implementation never reached an integration boundary.
Rejected because final assembly did not lack an assigned owner; the parent remained responsible and began the project skeleton, but the run timed out before a complete packageable candidate existed.
Rejected because the parent/workflow owned the end-to-end process; the failed transition from research to complete build was caused by broad fan-out budget exhaustion, not absent pipeline ownership.
Rejected because no single mandatory preflight gate blocked all work; the parent probed and implemented while workflow children ran.
Rejected because the parallel run was not only a serial first-phase investigation; child probes overlapped with parent implementation work and later critique/follow-up starts.

Rejected as the nearest load-imbalance competitor because the concrete allocation boundary was excessive breadth/retries across many live children consuming budget, making Fan-out Budget Exhaustion more specific.

The parallel parent launched a workflow that mapped every behavioral dimension into child agents and then critics/follow-ups. The workflow consumed 2,216,252 child tokens and 1,038 child tool calls, logged many stalled retries, and ended killed with most agents still in progress, while the parent only reached a partial Go skeleton before the 2,400 second budget expired. This is a realized process consequence in the parallel run, but not an outcome differential because the serial control also failed compilation.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad workflow consumed the available child budget and was killed before broad exploration, critique, and follow-up could be reduced into a finished, compileable submitted implementation.
candidates.near_match_reason: Critical-path starvation is less specific here because the directly evidenced episode is collective fan-out breadth plus retries exhausting the finite run budget, not merely too little capacity on one implementation path.

candidates.reason: Rejected because no single child is uniquely proven to have an overbroad dominant assignment; the adverse episode was collective breadth and retry churn across many dimensions.

Rejected because the child prompts included task rules, environment facts, scratch/report paths, and detailed dimension-specific acceptance requirements; failed closure came from scope breadth rather than an omitted known requirement in a specific brief.
Rejected because the children were delegated independent behavioral reports, not mutually dependent implementation components with incompatible APIs or file contracts.
Rejected because there is no direct before/after transfer where a known finding disappeared through summary or compaction and caused rework.

Rejected because some returned summaries were lengthy but the key problem was that most workflow work never completed; no available completed handoff is shown to be too bulky for a receiver to reduce.
Rejected because no receiver acted on superseded workspace, requirement, or dependency state from a stale child result.
Rejected because there are no incompatible child reports shown as simultaneously available and left unadjudicated at a decision point.
Rejected because the parent did not present the whole task as complete; final.txt is empty and official status shows timeout/compile failure rather than an unsupported acceptance decision.
Rejected because workflow retries followed stall detection within the same broad fan-out; there is no replacement attempt that repeated prior work because reusable checkpoints were withheld.

Rejected because cancelled/stalled children are part of the retained fan-out exhaustion chain; there is no independent required child failure with a separate takeover opportunity.

Rejected because the completed cli-flags and separate-named reports appear in the workflow journal, but there is no parent decision point showing the parent received and inconsistently ignored a concrete completed result.
Rejected because the parent continued probing and writing source while children ran; the timeout was not simply waiting without inspecting available progress.
Rejected because concurrent children wrote scratch findings under /tmp, while parent wrote /workspace source; no competing overlapping source design across final files is directly evidenced.
Rejected because there is no evidence of two live agents editing the same source or configuration file.
Rejected because no actor is shown replacing or deleting library/module/configuration source owned by another actor.

Rejected because artifact validation lists the final tree but does not show a broad cleanup/rebuild overwriting another actor's final-tree work.
Rejected because child writes were isolated to /tmp/probe and /tmp/findings, and no concrete unstable provenance problem from multiple live agents writing the final workspace is shown.
Rejected because no generated child artifact or temporary/cache file is shown being consumed by another actor as stable reference input in a way that contaminated probing or verification.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination, Missing Verifier Return, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were not retained separately because they describe downstream symptoms of the same killed broad-fanout workflow.

Critical-Path Starvation and Oversized Child Task were rejected because the evidence points to collective fan-out breadth and retries rather than a separate critical path or one dominant child assignment.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only Fan-out Budget Exhaustion cleared the paired retention gate.
